scope: Proposition 2.1 (Positive coefficient rule) of the manuscript “Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections” (preprints/Virasoro-Constraints-for-Projective-Complete-Intersections-September-24-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 065 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 01a2df978a0bfae2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: A labelled coefficient of LX k ZX, for fixed k > 0, is a finite linear combination of the following operations on the disconnected Gromov–Witten tensors: (i) add one special unit marking, with prescribed descendant and RX-powers; (ii) act on one existing marking, changing its descendant exponent and applying an RX-power, with a coefficient polynomial in its first Hodge degree; (iii) add two markings joined by the coevaluation of ( , )X, with descendant powers, first-Hodge- degree polynomials, and RX-powers on its legs; (iv) remove two primary markings, leaving their two cohomology inputs in the classical pairing with Rk+1 X , multiplied by the remaining disconnected Gromov–Witten tensor. The numerical coefficients and genus powers are universal for targets of fixed dimension. At most two existing labels are used nonordinarily in one summand.
